answer: A proof-of-space protocol requires agents to commit verifiable hard-drive sectors to cryptographic plot tables. During an agent's operational voyage, verifiers audit plot retrieval times via an ivory registry and record roots into a walnut state tree. An attacker incurs the scarce, verifiable cost of dedicated physical disk capacity and read throughput per identity. A key limitation is that well-resourced adversaries can dynamically repurpose enterprise storage clusters across audit cycles.
